_comment: Throughput baseline for bench/regression-gate.sh. Raising this is a
deliberate act in a commit, the same as the documentation ratchets in
tests/docs_drift_test.rs. Do NOT lower it to make a red run pass: that
records a regression as the new normal, which is precisely how the 0.5.84
drop survived four releases.
The figure is 4-core offline reconstruction over the fixed-state 535k
corpus that bench/carrier.py generates (5000 calls, 100 Call-IDs, 200
streams). Four cores is both the peak of the curve and its most
reproducible point.
Measured on a LOCAL release build of the recorded commit, not on a release
artifact -- the gate has to catch a regression the day it lands, not once
it has shipped.
WHY THIS RAISE IS LARGE, AND WHAT IT COST TO LEARN. The previous entry
recorded 0.5.104's 2.28M and was never raised when 0.5.108 lifted the real
figure to 3.30M by mapping the capture file. docs/benchmarks.md was updated
to 3.25M that day; this file was not. So when 0.5.118 introduced a defect
that cost 27% -- is_merged read the ENTIRE capture into memory before
rejecting it on the first four bytes -- the tool fell to 2.40M, which is
105% of a baseline recorded four releases earlier. The gate passed. It
passed on every release from 0.5.118 to 0.5.121 while the shipped binary
was a quarter slower than the page advertising it.
That is this file's own warning, come true a second time, and it is left
in the paragraph below because it was already written down and still did
not prevent this. The lesson is narrower than 'keep it fresh': a raise in
docs/benchmarks.md and a raise here are the SAME event, and doing one
without the other converts a 20% gate into a 31% one silently. Whoever
re-measures that page re-measures this file in the same commit.

measured.host: NVIDIA Jetson Thor devboard (aarch64), 14 cores, PREEMPT_RT, idle
measured.method: median-of-5 after one discarded warmup, three replicates
measured.idle_gate: vmstat id >= 96% and no toolchain build process; 90% would permit 1.4 busy cores on a 14-core host
measured._note: Baseline set to the LOWEST replicate, not the median, so the floor derived from it cannot sit above a figure this host actually produces.

_floor_rationale: The regression this gate exists to catch was 40%. Run-to-run spread is ~2%
on an idle host and ~10% when something else shares it, so 20% sits clear
of both. A tighter band on a runner that also serves CI would be flaky in
the direction that gets a gate muted, and a muted gate catches nothing.
The floor is 2.60M. Checked against the numbers that matter here: the
0.5.118 regression measured 2.40M, which is 74% and trips it -- the whole
point of the raise. 0.5.117's 3.29M is 101% and does not.
Note what the raise fixed, twice now. While this file baselined 0.5.89's
1.89M, the floor sat at 1.51M against a tool running at 2.28M -- a 34% drop
would have passed a gate whose stated band is 20%. While it baselined
0.5.104's 2.28M, a tool running at 3.30M could lose 27% and pass. A stale
baseline does not merely under-report; it silently widens the band it
